newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt mixed in U.S., beholden to Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt mixed in U.S., beholden to Treasuries.

text.p: Swayed by erratic moves in U.S. Treasuries, emerging market debts turned in a mixed performance on Wednesday.

Profit-taking after Tuesday's strong gains drove the trade. "The Treasuries have pulled Latin Bradies up," said a Brady trader, referring to Tuesday's rally, in which Bradies even outperformed Treasuries.

The market also used Wednesday as an opportunity to square positions before Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report. A Reuters poll showed economists expected an increase of 212,000 new jobs in October following September's fall of 40,000.
But the gains were far from making up for the lost momentum in the market's recent retracement, and traders were inclined to play defensively, he said.
Unless the Treasuries continue sprinting higher, the Bradies are unlikely to retest recent highs on their own strength, the trader said.
Most Latin papers suffered minor losses, with Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR trading 58-5/8 bid, down 3/8 on the day, and Brazil C BR8D14=RR 68-1/2 bid, down 1/4.
But the undertone of Argentine papers was more positive than the Brazilian, said Richard Segal, head of emerging markets fixed income research at Santander Investment.
Argentine industrial production in September rose 11.1 percent, year-on-year, despite the strike days, showing the economic recovery was more robust than expected, he said.
Brazil's stubbornly high trade deficit, on the other hand, has caused concerns, as reflected in the disappointing performance of its five-year $750 million global bond priced on Monday, Segal said.
East European and Russian debts, which -- except Poland -- did not participate fully in Tuesday's rally, played catch-up ending mostly higher.
Bulgaria FLRB BGFLIRG=RR rose 1/2 to 32 bid, and Russia's dollar-denominated Vnesh loan RUVNUSLNS=RR added 3/8 to 73-1/8 bid.
